description:
100 / 100k pre-hashed u64s, p=14. ex_data_sketch 0.10.3 at the backend layer: baseline Backend.Pure.hll_update_many(state, [u64], p: 14), NIF column Backend.Rust.hll_update_many (packs the list to a binary in Elixir; copies registers twice per call, confirmed in hll.rs, so the per-call copy is like for like). defk packs the same list end to end. Public HLL.update_many (10k chunking, raw hashing path) out. Agreement: byte-identical state binary.

Evidence bar (from defk-dtw.4/defk-dtw.15): script examples/<name>.exs with Mix.install of the pinned anchor package; the anchor's Elixir version is the first baseline and must be optimised further in Elixir before the verdict counts (what was tried listed in the header; baseline: :optimized); realistic size declared in the header before any numbers; workload verdict at the realistic size, other size beside; ~6-point geometric sweep with crossover (smallest size where defk >= 2x, or none), skipped if a large run exceeds ~1 min; NIF timing and responsiveness (max and p99 1 ms tick gap, one scheduler, large size, for Elixir/defk/NIF) via Defk.Bench.report/1; Elixir, defk and NIF outputs must agree (failure fails the script); quiet-machine run_all.exs; row added to examples/README.md.

comments.text: Per defk-i2e: writes to the input register array are legal (copied once before the first write), so update_many can be written as plain regs[i] = ... and return regs. Blocked on defk-auo.

Done on branch defk-9p6.15/hll-update-many (5aa8569, merge 6b98bb7, 6e8db76): examples/hll_update_many.exs, README row under 'Where defk helps'. PROVISIONAL, measured under load (pcm/cosine agents running). Rust backend: precompiled NIF installed fine (rustler_precompiled, aarch64-apple-darwin). Pure backend read: bucket = h >>> (64-p), rank = clz of the low 64-p bits counted in a (64-p)-bit field + 1 (all-zero field -> 64-p+1); state = 4-byte header + 2^p u8 registers. Kernel: for h <- hashes, state[4 + bsr(h, bits)] = max(.., min(clz(band(bsl(h,p), mask64)), bits) + 1), input state copied once; plain loop (defk-fun not hit). Realistic size 100k hashes, p=14, sketch pre-filled with 50k; other size 100. Elixir variants (best of 7, ms at 100 / 1k / 10k / 100k): E0 anchor Pure 0.044/0.17/3.1/17-24; E1 top-down rank 0.036/0.10/2.5/10.3; E2 sorted int keys + splice 0.019/0.058/1.6/9.2 (baseline <5k); E3 :atomics + one rebuild 0.48/0.21/0.50/3.3 (baseline >=5k); E4 bit-syntax split 4.0 at 100k; E5 :array 5.4; E6 tuple put_elem 8.5 at 10k (not run beyond); E7 per-hash bit-syntax update 0.026 at 100, 8.6 at 100k; E8 parallel tasks 4.4. Verdict at 100k: Elixir 3.4-3.5 ms, defk 0.36-0.38 ms (kernel 0.07, pack the rest), 9.2-9.4x good; 100 hashes 10-15x (mean of 5000 calls). Pack variants at 100k: append 4/iter 0.28, append 1/iter 1.1, comprehension 2.4, Enum.map+iodata 2.3. Sweep 100..100k x3.16: 2.7-5x, 7x, 12x, 15-17x, 15x, 13-14x, 3.2x (the 100k sweep point is 1.06 ms: GC artefact, filed defk-9p6.27); crossover 100. NIF Backend.Rust 2.55-2.8 ms at 100k (defk 6.9-7.4x; its Enum.map+iodata pack is 2.3 ms); NIF fed defk's pack 0.46 ms, level with defk. Tick gaps 100k one scheduler: ~2 ms max/p99 for all three (floor; NIF dirty >10k). Agreement: byte-identical state across 8 Elixir variants, baseline, defk, Elixir mode, NIF, NIF+defk pack; p=4/10/14/16, empty/filled state, edge hashes, random batches; mismatch halts. mix ci green after merging main (1276 passed).
